item.title: Colts coach Shane Steichen said he does not expect WR Alec Pierce (ankle) to resume practicing this week.
item.description:
Alec Pierce IND Wide Receiver

According to The Athletic’s James Boyd, this means Pierce will miss the entirety of the Colts’ training camp program. Tough break. Pierce has roughly one month to resume practicing and ramp up enough to play in Week 1 against the Ravens. He was supposed to be diversifying his route tree in order to take on a larger offensive role. Instead, he is stuck rehabbing during preseason play. Pierce is a very risky pick in fantasy right now.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Cowboys have explored free agent cornerback options, and CB Adoree’ Jackson is a “name to watch.”
item.description:
Adoree' Jackson

Fowler reminds us that Cowboys DC Christian was the Eagles’ passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach from 2024-25, and Jackson spent last year playing for him in Philadelphia. A reunion could make sense, and Jackson worked out for the Cowboys back in May. Jackson notched six pass breakups and one interception last year, and reportedly has interest from a few teams. Stay tuned.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Cowboys signed EDGE Von Miller, formerly of the Commanders.
item.description:
Von Miller DAL Linebacker

Miller, 37, had a very productive year with the Commanders last year. PFF credits him with 36 quarterback pressures, 10 sacks and 14 tackles. Miller should make a notable impact on passing downs and still has some early-down utility as well. Miller and the team reportedly agreed to a one-year pact. It’s a smart signing for Dallas.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Stephen Holder reports that “signs continue to point to” the Colts keeping QB Anthony Richardson on the roster in 2026.
item.description:
Anthony Richardson IND Quarterback

Holder cites comments made by Colts assistant general manager Ed Dodds today. Dodds did not come right out and share the team’s plans, but when asked about Richardson’s status, he stressed the importance of having three quarterbacks on the roster. The Colts’ quarterback position group was so banged up last year that they brought Philip Rivers out of retirement. Recouping value for Richardson has its merits, but the Colts intend to compete this season. Keeping the quarterback room deep makes sense.

Source: ESPN

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love “is dealing with a high ankle sprain.”
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

We suspected this might be the case when Schefter’s colleague, Jeremy Fowler, reported earlier today that the team is “hopeful” Love can play in Week 1 against the Chargers. This evening, Schefter echoed that phrasing, saying the team is “hoping” he can return in time for the season opener. Love has just under a month to get healthy. He remains a high-upside pick, but RB Tyler Allgeier should be targeted as a bench stash. The Cardinals surprisingly gave Love 14 touches in Thursday’s preseason game. One imagines they might be more conservative with his early-season touch count, assuming he is able to play, but only coach Mike LaFleur knows for sure.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Texans WR Jaylin Noel (hamstring/finger) will be out for “a few weeks” after suffering “a little bit of a setback.”
item.description:
Jaylin Noel HOU Wide Receiver

NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson noted earlier today that Noel was not participating in practice due to a finger injury, which he suffered in July, and a recent hamstring injury. It turns out Noel’s recent hamstring injury is actually a re-injury. Fellow second-year WR Jayden Higgins has the inside track to the WR2 role. Noel was set to compete with Xavier Hutchinson and WR Tank Dell for the WR3 gig. Instead, he is losing valuable preseason reps. Noel might be best viewed as an early-season waiver wire add.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: ESPN’s Turron Davenport reports that Titans OC Brian Daboll’s intent to improve on third down was a “key reason” for signing WR Wan’Dale Robinson.
item.description:
Wan'Dale Robinson TEN Wide Receiver

Davenport penned a lengthy piece detailing how OC Brian Daboll is focused on developing QB Cam Ward’s play on third down, in the red zone and in the two-minute drill. This is pretty straightforward. Those are all high-leverage situations, so harping on Ward’s performance there makes sense. Robinson played on all three drives in the Titans’ first preseason game while veteran Calvin Ridley was on the field for one. Rookie WR Carnell Tate was on the field for the first and third drives. A featured role on third downs could help Robinson return FLEX value — he’s certainly being paid like he is going to be featured.

Source: ESPN

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Vikings LB Jamal Adams suffered a season-ending knee injury in Saturday’s preseason game against the Giants.
item.description:
Jamal Adams MIN Linebacker

Adams, 30, has had some tough injury luck over the course of his career. He was set to play on a one-year, $1.3 million contract this season. He totaled 38 tackles, seven quarterback pressures and one sack with the Raiders last year.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Free agent DE Marcus Davenport worked out for the Bears on Sunday.
item.description:
Marcus Davenport

Davenport, 29, totaled just seven quarterback pressures and one sack for the Lions last year. He is likely best suited to a rotational role at this point. The Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs notes that Davenport began his career with the Saints in 2018, playing for the Bears’ current defensive coordinator, Dennis Allen.

Source: Brad Biggs

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Bears RB Kyle Monangai (knee) is believed to be “fine” after undergoing initial testing.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

According to Schefter, initial tests indicate Monangai’s knee is structurally sound. He is scheduled to undergo an MRI to confirm the results, but it sounds like Monangai avoided suffering a consequential injury. This is great news for the second-year back, who warrants standalone FLEX treatment if his knee checks out. Starting RB D’Andre Swift can easily shoulder a few extra touches if Monangai needs to be eased into action next month.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Raiders signed WR Noah Brown, formerly of the Commanders.
item.description:
Noah Brown LV Wide Receiver

Brown, 30, dealt with knee, groin and rib injuries last season. He profiles as a rotational player at this point in his career, but the Raiders’ wide receiver depth chart is fairly thin. He is unlikely to be fantasy-relevant, though he can help out at the team level. The Raiders correspondingly released DT Benito Jones.

Source: Las Vegas Raiders

item.title: FOX Sports’ Ralph Vacchiano believes RB Rico Dowdle “should end up as the workhorse in the Steelers’ backfield” this year.
item.description:
Rico Dowdle PIT Running Back

Recent reporting from ESPN suggests the Steelers will employ a run-heavy approach this season. Vacchiano agrees and adds that Steelers coach Mike McCarthy believes Dowdle could help the team produce a strong running game this season. That said, Vacchiano also said that Dowdle and RB Jaylen Warren could form “a potent tandem,” so Vacchiano may only be indicating that Dowdle will be the team’s primary rusher while Warren changes the pace and plays on passing downs. Both players sit in the fringe RB2/FLEX barrel right now.

Source: FOX Sports

item.title: Bears activated OT Ozzy Trapilo (knee) from the physically unable to perform list on Sunday.
item.description:
Ozzy Trapilo CHI Offensive Lineman

Trapilo even resumed practicing today. This is quite an accomplishment. Trapilo suffered a season-ending patellar tendon rupture in the Bears’ Wild Card Round win over the Packers last year. He was expected to be sidelined “deep into next year,’ per general manager Ryan Poles, but Trapilo’s recovery has apparently gone very well. Trapilo proved himself as a capable pass protector and run blocker. He may need a while to ramp up, but the Bears are currently hosting a competition for the left tackle job. Veteran OT Braxton Jones has been sidelined with an undisclosed injury, but coach Ben Johnson recently said he could resume practicing this week. He got in one limited session last week.

Source: Brad Biggs

item.title: 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey (tightness) did not practice on Sunday.
item.description:
Christian McCaffrey SF Running Back

The 49ers do not have to disclose any details here, so we just have to wait until McCaffrey either tells us himself or retakes the practice field. The veteran running back has plenty of time to get right for Week 1. We are not overly concerned. He remains a high-end RB1 for the 2026 season, but we will provide an update whenever we get one.

Source: Cam Inman

item.title: Bears RB Kyle Monangai left practice early on Sunday after suffering an apparent right knee injury.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

According to the Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs, Monangai “got tangled up” with DT Grady Jarrett when the injury occurred. The second-year running back was able to walk off the field and into the locker room under his own power. The fact that the cart was not needed might be a good sign, but unfortunately, we are simply in wait-and-see mode for the time being. Bears RBs Roschon Johnson and Brittain Brown sit on the depth chart behind him. Starting RB D’Andre Swift could absorb a big chunk of Monangai’s workload if he misses time.

Source: Brad Biggs

item.title: 49ers TE George Kittle (Achilles) said he is “nearing a return to practice” and has “a chance” to play in Week 1 against the Rams.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

Kittle is “very confident” he will be activated from the active/PUP list before Week 1, meaning he should resume playing sometime in Weeks 1-4. The veteran tight end has not yet resumed practicing, but “hinted he’d be back at practice shortly but declined to give a timeline,” per The Athletic’s Matt Barrows. Kittle said that he is running and hitting top speeds while doing so. The 49ers are scheduled to fly out for the Week 1 game in Melbourne, Australia roughly one week before the game. Kittle said that the next couple of weeks will determine whether he joins his teammates on that flight. From the way Kittle is discussing his recovery, it almost sounds like he expects to play in Week 2 at the latest, though that is purely an interpretive conclusion. Whether Kittle returns to form as a post-catch dominator remains to be seen, but the 32-year-old remains a top-12 player at his position at this time.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Packers TE Tucker Kraft (knee) said the team will “probably” keep him on a snap count until halfway through the 2026 season.
item.description:
Tucker Kraft GB Tight End

Kraft is recovering from a season-ending ACL tear. He is on track to play in Week 1. Easing him into action before “sending [him] to the wolves” partway through the year, as Kraft says, makes sense. Kraft proved himself to be a top-tier real-life tight end and a locked-in TE1 in fantasy last year. He can still return TE1 numbers while playing on a snap count, likely receiving a few first-read passes that are designed with his post-catch skill set in mind. These comments should not impact his ADP negatively. For what it’s worth, Kraft also said that he is hoping to play his normal allotment of snaps in Week 1. The team may simply choose to take a conservative approach. Kraft notably resumed participating in 11-on-11 drills today.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Cardinals are “still hopeful” that RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will be ready for Week 1 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

The language regarding Love’s ankle injury continues to evolve. The team initially said the No. 3 overall pick could have re-entered Thursday’s preseason game if necessary. Coach Mike LaFleur later said Love would need at least a week off. On the plus side, Fowler referred to Love as the team’s “soon-to-be lead back,” furthering the notion that some of the training camp rotation hubbub was perhaps inaccurate. Love has time to recover and play productively this season. His recovery is simply worth tracking right now.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler believes Browns coach Todd Monken could name a starter after “at some point” after Saturday’s preseason game against the Bills.
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

Both Fowler and his colleague, Herm Edwards, complimented QB Deshaun Watson’s recent performances in both practice and preseason play. Per Fowler, Watson “has some momentum, not all of the momentum” at this time. His competitor, QB Shedeur Sanders, will start against the Bills this weekend.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Titans signed RB Dominic Richardson, formerly of the Cowboys.
item.description:
Dominic Richardson TEN Running Back

Richardson is a 2026 undrafted free agent. The Titans also signed TE Matt Lauter. They correspondingly placed DE Jaylen Harrell and TE Jaren Kanak on injured reserve.

Source: Jim Wyatt

item.title: Texans WR Tank Dell did not practice on Sunday.
item.description:
Tank Dell HOU Wide Receiver

NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson listed the Texans players who were not practicing on Sunday. Dell was the only player who was not listed with an injury designation, so it seems likely that this is just a rest day. The Texans are easing Dell, 26, back into action following a lengthy absence stemming from a multi-ligament knee injury suffered in 2024. Dell’s range of potential outcomes remains wide. He may be best suited to a complementary, rotational role.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Texans WR Jaylin Noel (hamstring/finger) did not practice on Sunday.
item.description:
Jaylin Noel HOU Wide Receiver

Noel has been dealing with the pinky finger issue since late July, but the hamstring is a recent injury. The second-year wide receiver would ideally be competing for the WR3 role right now, and losing reps could slow him down. He is a risky dart throw, but he flashed talent at times in his rookie season.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Dolphins QB Quinn Ewers suffered a groin injury in Friday’s preseason game against the Commanders.
item.description:
Quinn Ewers MIA Quarterback

The Dolphins signed QB Mark Gronowski after Ewers picked up the injury. Ewers is the Dolphins’ primary backup, so the team was a little short-staffed for the remaining preseason games. Dolphins backup OT Jamaree Salyer reportedly suffered a season-ending injury and was placed on injured reserve. The Dolphins also waived CB Ethan Robinson and signed LB Cam Riley.

Source: David Furones

item.title: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Jeremy McNichols (quad) will be sidelined a few weeks.
item.description:
Jeremy McNichols WAS Running Back

McNichols probably is no higher than fourth on the depth chart in Washington behind ‘Bill,’ Rachaad White, and Kaytron Allen. Missing time due to injury doesn’t bode well for him making the initial 53-man roster.

Source: Ben Standig

item.title: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports Isaiah Likely is leading all first-team receivers in catches “by a wide margin.”
item.description:
Isaiah Likely NYG Tight End

With Malik Nabers still off the field, that’s a given. Still, Likely finds himself as barely a top-12 tight end by ADP. The argument could be made that he belongs closer to the top 10. “Given the way [Jaxson] Dart likes to throw to his tight ends, it suggests that Likely is in for a breakout season given the chemistry they already have developed,” Raanan concludes.

Source: ESPN

item.title: ESPN’s Ryan McFadden believes Malik Benson has been the Raiders top performer at training camp and could overtake Jack Bech as Las Vegas’ third wideout.
item.description:
Malik Benson LV Wide Receiver

Benson has been inundated with buzz this offseason. He caught two balls for 26 yards on four targets in Las Vegas’ first preseason game and reportedly has a strong connection with Fernando Mendoza. Outside of Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty it’s been hard to recommend any Raiders skill position player in fantasy circles this year; perhaps the sixth-round pick can step into a real target role given the lack of competition around him.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Packers EDGE Lukas Van Ness (shoulder) is not practicing on Sunday.
item.description:
Lukas Van Ness GB Defensive End

Severity is unknown at this point and the injury didn’t happen at the practice, so we’ll await further team comment before getting too worried. The Packers definitely can’t afford to have Van Ness down with Micah Parsons already on pace to miss the first month of the season.

Source: Matt Schneidman

item.title: ESPN’s Michael DiRocco believes Parker Washington has “established himself” as the Jaguars’ WR1.
item.description:
Parker Washington

Washington has been Lawrence’s “favorite target, and he always seems to be open” DiRocco notes. The Jaguars main pass catchers are pretty close in ADP, with Washington leading the way at WR31 and Brian Thomas Jr. at WR33. This would seem to be an argument to trust Washington as a true WR2/WR3 option — and everything we’ve gotten on Washington this offseason from beat writers has been overwhelmingly positive.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Bears assistant head coach Antwaan Randle El called offensive plays in the second half of Chicago’s 34-10 win over the Browns in Week 1 of the preseason.
item.description:
Antwaan Randle El CHI Coaching Staff

It certainly can’t hurt his case for head coaching work should the Bears offense continue to play well above the league average. Randle El’s offensive playcalling produced 235 yards and 24 points in the second half.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Marcus Mariota (knee) sprained his MCL and will miss the remainder of the preseason.
item.description:
Marcus Mariota WAS Quarterback

Frankly, a pretty good update considering how quickly Mariota exited the field on Friday. The Commanders will likely pick up another quarterback to help navigate the final two weeks of the preseason. Mariota will be the backup for the season opener if healthy.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Cyrus Allen caught 2-of-5 targets for 20 yards in Kansas City’s first preseason game.
item.description:
Cyrus Allen KC Wide Receiver

The good news is that Allen worked with the starters in the slot. The bad news is that he worked well into the second half in the first preseason game while leading the team in targets. He’s clearly the highest-upside stash receiver of the group, but playing deep into the first preseason game isn’t a great sign for his chances of early playing time.

item.title: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Emmett Johnson was “one of the positives coming out of” their first preseason game.
item.description:
Emmett Johnson KC Running Back

Johnson had 12 carries for 59 yards and three catches for 10 yards against the Rams. While we’ve seen a little camp buzz about Johnson, The Athletic’s Jesse Newell presents this as a step forward for Johnson who “has been running with the fourth-string offense most of training camp.” He’s still probably the best back to have rostered in the event of a Kenneth Walker injury, but this isn’t such an important role that the backup necessarily needs to be rostered in standard redraft leagues.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Browns coach Todd Monken said Deshaun Watson “functioned at a high level” against the Bears in their preseason opener.
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

We’d normally skip right past this, but it’s a notable quote given the open competition for the starting quarterback job. It would seem to imply that Watson is in the lead. “It was so cool to watch him play. I get all of the frustration by fans, himself (with the past), but for him to come back and work like he did is an unbelievable credit to him,” Monken said. It sounds like Monken will continue the competition through the second week of the preseason, but there’s already a lean here.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: The Athletic’s Zach Rosenblatt believes Isaiah Williams “appears to have overtaken” Omar Cooper for the starting slot receiver job.
item.description:
Isaiah Williams NYJ Wide Receiver

We blurbed about Cooper playing deep into the preseason game on Friday — never a great sign — and this backs that up. Williams, an outstanding return man in his rookie season, enters the deep sleeper conversation at wideout.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: The Athletic’s Zach Rosenblatt believes Cade Klubnik is the favorite for the Jets backup quarterback job.
item.description:
Cade Klubnik NYJ Quarterback

Klubnik played two series with the starters in the first preseason game before giving way to Bailey Zappe and Brady Cook, going 5-of-7 for 56 yards. “He has some moxie to him,” Jets coach Aaron Glenn said. “He’s very confident, he’s confident in his arm, confident in his ability to elude and make plays with his feet. His ability to be able to come out and operate with the first group the way he did, I thought, was outstanding.” Given how Jets quarterbacking has gone over the past few years and Geno Smith’s age, Klubnik will likely find himself in a starting lineup at some point this season if he can stay healthy.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Bills C Connor McGovern (undisclosed) is dealing with a multi-week injury.
item.description:
Connor McGovern BUF Offensive Lineman

It “should be a few more weeks,” for McGovern, whose goal is to be ready for the start of the season. Lloyd Cushenberry would take over at center if McGovern can’t be ready for Week 1 against the Texans.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said there’s no timeline for James Conner (ankle) to return to 11-on-11 work.
item.description:
James Conner ARI Running Back

It doesn’t sound like Conner has a great chance of being available for Week 1, and if he’s not yet able to fully practice it’s certainly on the table for Conner to start the year on injured reserve or the reserve/PUP list. Conner took a paycut this offseason and is due $2.35 million guaranteed in 2026 after suffering a season-ending injury in Week 3 last year.

Source: Darren Urban

item.title: Cardinals placed OG Chase Bisontis (knee) on season-ending injured reserve.
item.description:
Chase Bisontis ARI Guard

He tore his MCL against the Raiders on Thursday night in the team’s first preseason game. "(Chase) will be out for a good amount of time, if not the whole year,” Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said. “Sucks for him. Always think about the player first. Sucks for the Cardinals too, He’s a good player but more importantly you hate it for the player.” The second-round pick will rehab and get ready for a return in 2027.

Source: Cardinals.com

item.title: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Kyler Gordon (calf) has a timeline to return of “unknown.”
item.description:
Kyler Gordon CHI Defensive Back

It certainly looks like Gordon will hit reserve/PUP or injured reserve before the start of the season while he deals with this long-term calf injury. This makes both the Bears coach and GM telling you they’re frustrated with the situation.

Source: Courtney Cronin

item.title: Malachi Fields caught 3-of-3 targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in the first week of the preseason against the Vikings.
item.description:
Malachi Fields NYG Wide Receiver

It’s a game that The Athletic’s Dan Duggan says “strengthened his push for the No. 2 receiver job.” His touchdown pass was from Jaxson Dart, but he was one of several receivers getting first-team snaps. It’s hard to believe Fields will be relevant early in 12-team redraft leagues unless Malik Nabers suffers a setback, but he’s squarely on the fantasy radar after a big camp.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Jonathon Brooks rushed three times for five yards, adding a nine-yard catch, in Carolina’s preseason opener against the Bills.
item.description:
Jonathon Brooks CAR Running Back

It was his first game action in 20 months. The Panthers’ offense, playing their starters three series, looked dead on arrival against the Bills on Saturday. But Brooks did start with Chuba Hubbard sidelined, validating the training camp drumbeat that he’d be in the mix early. He’s at least an interesting bench option in standard leagues at this point, and could perhaps turn into more.

item.title: Camden Brown caught 3-of-3 targets for 62 yards and two touchdowns in Saturday’s preseason win over the Seahawks.
item.description:
Camden Brown DAL Wide Receiver

Brown made an impact in his exhibition debut, and he connected with Sam Howell on a 39-year touchdown in the second quarter. His second score was far shorter but even more impressive; a one-handed stab in the back of the end zone. There’s a long way to go and Brown is anything but a lock to make the roster, but he’s been one of the stars of training camp, and he showed why Saturday evening. At the very least, he’s worth monitoring.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jalen Milroe completed 5-of-8 passes for 36 yards in Saturday’s preseason game against the Cowboys while adding 36 yards on five carries.
item.description:
Jalen Milroe SEA Quarterback

Milroe and Drew Lock split time in the first game of the preseason, and Lock was much more effective with a touchdown and 40 yards on 9-of-13 passing. That’s more insult to Milroe than compliment to Lock, to be fair. The second-year signal-caller showed off his upper-echelon speed, but held onto the ball too long, and struggled to get the ball down field. Milroe would be a tantalizing fantasy play because of his ability to scramble, but just isn’t a good enough passer to believe that’s going to come to fruition.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Ja’Kobi Lane caught 3-of-3 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in Saturday’s preseason contest against the Eagles.
item.description:
Ja'Kobi Lane BAL Wide Receiver

Lane has impressed in camp, and he snagged a 16-yard touchdown from fellow rookie Joe Fagnano for his first score of the season. The 80th pick of last year’s draft, Lane’s 6-foot-4 frame makes him a potential threat inside the 20, and it appears he’s going to get a chance to win the No. 3 receiving job. At the very least, Lane is worth monitoring in deeper formats.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Eli Stowers caught all three targets for 12 yards in Saturday’s preseason game against the Ravens.
item.description:
Eli Stowers PHI Tight End

Stowers was somewhat involved in the first half but the rookie tight end had a long gain of just six yards in the first exhibition game of the season. The 23-year-old has significant long-term upside because of his athleticism, but it’s very clear — at least early on — that Stowers has work to do before he’s a fantasy option in 2026.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Vikings LB Jamal Adams suffered a season-ending knee injury in Saturday’s preseason game against the Giants.
item.description:
Jamal Adams MIN Linebacker

Adams, 30, has had some tough injury luck over the course of his career. This is very unfortunate. Adams was set to play on a one-year, $1.3 million contract this season. He totaled 38 tackles, seven quarterback pressures and one sack with the Raiders last year.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Saints HC Kellen Moore said the team is “still in collection mode” regarding Jordyn Tyson’s hamstring injury
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

This comes a day after we learned that Tyson is seeking multiple opinions on the hamstring injury he suffered on Thursday. At some point, the Saints will have collected enough information to feel comfortable telling us about Tyson’s injury, but for now, we will continue to wait. The longer this goes on, the worse the news will feel. Hopefully this is something that will only sideline Tyson for a few weeks, but given his history of hamstring injuries, which slowed him during the pre-draft process, it wouldn’t be surprising if his absence extended into the regular season. Hopefully we’ll have a clear answer on his status soon.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Ty Simpson completed 21-of-25 passes for 190 yards and two touchdowns in Saturday’s preseason game against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Ty Simpson

Simpson played all but two drives for the Rams in this one, as Sean McVay gave his rookie first-rounder an extended first taste of NFL action. Simpson played about as clean of a game as one could have hoped for, avoiding sacks and turnovers while leading his team on three scoring drives. Simpson’s first touchdown pass came on a screen pass to running back Dean Conners, who took it into the end zone for the score. Later, Simpson connected with Conners on a two-yard score after he found a hole between two defenders to fit the ball into. We would expect Simpson to see another lengthy outing in next week’s game against the Saints.

item.title: Zach Wilson completed 11-of-16 passes for 145 yards and one touchdown in Saturday’s preseason game against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Zach Wilson NO Quarterback

Wilson took over in the second quarter for Spencer Rattler, who struggled mightily in his 2026 debut. Wilson, on the other hand, looked far more comfortable running the offense and completed four of his five pass attempts on distances of 10 or more air yards. He was a perfect 2-for-2 on passes of 20-plus yards. Wilson connected with tight end Oscar Delp on a one-yard pass for his lone touchdown of the day and led the Saints on two scoring drives. Given what we saw from both Wilson and Rattler today, it wouldn’t be surprising if Wilson pushes Rattler for the QB2 spot behind Tyler Shough.

item.title: Vikings HC Kevin O’Connell said the knee injury Jamal Adams suffered in Saturday’s preseason game against the Giants is “not good.”
item.description:
Jamal Adams MIN Linebacker

This doesn’t come as much of a surprise after O’Connell sounded disappointed when discussing Adams’ injury after halftime. The 10-year vet had made a switch to linebacker last season and signed with the Vikings last month in hopes of carving out a role in Brian Flores’ defense. Adams has an MRI scheduled for tomorrow, which will reveal the extent of the damage.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Spencer Rattler completed 8-of-11 passes for 42 yards in Saturday’s preseason game against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Spencer Rattler NO Quarterback

Rattler’s 3.8 yards per attempt won’t turn any heads, but the two sacks he took, one of which resulted in a lost fumble, might be enough to give Zach Wilson a chance at backup duties. Rattler didn’t complete a pass for more than nine yards on Saturday and will look to have a bounce-back performance in his next game, which is set for Saturday against the Rams.

item.title: Bills HC Joe Brady said DJ Moore was “good to go” after suffering an ankle injury in Saturday’s preseason game against the Panthers.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

Moore had his ankle rolled up on late in the fourth quarter and could be seen working with trainers on the sideline. Despite the scare, Moore told Brady after the game that he was “good to go,” suggesting there won’t be much to worry about going forward. Moore was impressive in his Bills debut, catching 3-of-4 targets for 61 yards in limited action.

item.title: KC Concepcion caught 3-of-4 passes for 27 yards in Saturday’s preseason game against the Bears, adding one carry for 14 yards and a touchdown.
item.description:
KC Concepcion KC Concepcion caught 3-of-4 passes for 27 yards in Saturday’s preseason game against the Bears, adding one carry for 14 yards and a touchdown.

Concepcion did a little bit of everything in this one, with his most notable play coming on a 14-yard rushing touchdown on a jet sweep. The rookie first-rounder also had an impressive 31-yard punt return that would have gone for more if not for a shoestring tackle by Hayden Large. Concepcion played on 24 offensive snaps, with all four of his targets coming from Deshaun Watson. It was a strong debut for the explosive rookie, who is among the more intriguing sleepers in fantasy drafts this season.
item.rw:position: Concepcion caught 3-of-4 passes for 27 yards in Saturday’s preseason game against the Bears, adding one carry for 14 yards and a touchdown.

item.title: Texans HC DeMeco Ryans said Graham Mertz suffered a torn ACL in Thursday’s preseason game against the Chargers.
item.description:
Graham Mertz HOU Quarterback

This one was expected after the team said it feared Mertz suffered a torn ACL shortly after the game. Mertz joined the Texans as a rookie UDFA in 2025. He made the roster as the team’s third-string QB but did not attempt a pass. He will now be placed on injured reserve, ending his 2026 season. In a corresponding move, the Texans signed veteran QB Brett Rypien to the roster.

item.title: Shedeur Sanders completed 6-of-11 passes for 79 yards and an interception in Saturday’s preseason game against the Bears.
item.description:
Shedeur Sanders CLE Quarterback

Playing with and against backups, Sanders started the second half for the Browns and came out with two solid throws. His first attempt was a 24-yard completion to Gage Larvadain, and he connected with wide receiver Luke Floriea on a nicely thrown deep ball for a 35-yard gain to convert a third-and-13 a few plays later. Unfortunately for Sanders, he managed just 20 yards on his next eight throws, with multiple passes being batted down at the line of scrimmage and his last throw being picked off on an errant pass that sailed well beyond his receiver. Both Sanders and Deshaun Watson committed turnovers in this one. Sanders is scheduled to make the start in the Browns’ next preseason game, which comes on Saturday at home against the Bills.

item.title: Vikings LB Jamal Adams (undisclosed) exited in the second quarter of Saturday’s preseason game against the Giants.
item.description:
Jamal Adams MIN Linebacker

It was a non-contact injury for Adams, who is the latest player to fall victim to the MetLife Stadium turf. The veteran linebacker was seen holding his right leg after going down on the play, and head coach Kevin O’Connell said after halftime that the Vikings are “going to miss him.” O’Connell didn’t say Adams’ injury was a season-ender, but his tone suggested his 2026 season could be over. We’ll get more information on this soon, but it’s a brutal blow to Adams, who was carving out a nice role in Brian Flores’ defense.

item.title: Keon Coleman caught 3-of-4 targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in Saturday’s preseason game against the Panthers.
item.description:
Keon Coleman BUF Wide Receiver

Coleman took the field with the starters on Saturday and also spent some time with the second team offense. Coleman scored the first unofficial touchdown at the new Highmark Stadium. Josh Allen evaded pressure in the backfield to find Coleman in the end zone for a nine-yard score, while backup Kyle Allen connected with Coleman twice. It’s been a challenging year and a half for Coleman, who was a healthy scratch for a few games last season. The Bills remain committed to giving Coleman a chance to succeed. This decent showing in limited preseason action is an encouraging sign.

item.title: Deshaun Watson completed 11-of-15 passes for 126 yards in Saturday’s preseason game against the Bears.
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

It was an up-and-down outing for Watson, who led two scoring drives in the first half. At times, Watson looked on point and decisive with his throws. On the lone touchdown drive he led, Watson went 4-for-4 passing, with his biggest play coming on a 43-yard screen pass to Dylan Sampson. Unfortunately, he also lost a fumble on a strip sack by Jamree Kromah and went three-and-out during a two-minute drill. It was exactly the kind of performance we expected to see based on reports of how the Browns’ QB battle has gone so far this offseason.

item.title: DJ Moore caught 3-of-4 targets for 61 yards Saturday’s preseason game against the Panthers.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

Moore’s first reception of the day came on a shallow crossing route that he turned upfield for a 32-yard gain. The new No. 1 target for Josh Allen would later haul in passes of 11 and 18 yards, but left the game with an apparent right ankle injury after having his leg rolled up on by a defender. Moore walked off under his own power and appeared in good spirits on the sideline, but we’ll likely get a better sense of his status after the game. Moore only ran six routes in this one, but his usage was very encouraging. It wouldn’t be surprising if we saw his ADP jump up a bit as a result of this strong first showing.

item.title: Jaxson Dart completed 3-of-4 passes for 26 yards and a touchdown in Saturday’s preseason game against the Vikings.
item.description:
Jaxson Dart NYG Quarterback

Dart made a trip to the blue medical tent at the end of the first quarter after going down hard on a sack from Vikings safety Jay Ward. After clearing concussion protocol, Dart would return to the field and fire a 15-yard touchdown pass to rookie Malachi Fields in the end zone. It would be the final play of the day for Dart, who took two sacks on the afternoon and didn’t add anything on the ground. While it’s good news to hear Dart cleared protocol, the visit to the tent is concerning for a player who was evaluated five times in 10 games for a concussion last season.

item.title: Steelers HC Mike McCarthy told reporters WR DK Metcalf and WR Michael Pittman won’t practice this week.
item.description:
DK Metcalf PIT Wide Receiver

Both receivers are set to miss the Steelers’ upcoming preseason game against the Jets with undisclosed injuries. Without both starting wide receivers, you can expect Aaron Rodgers to sit out as well. Without much practice time remaining, the next time we see the Steelers’ starting offense very well may be in the regular season.

item.title: Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is out for at least a week.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

Love came out of the Cardinals preseason game on Thursday with an ankle injury. HC Mike LaFluer said after the game that Love could have returned. On Saturday morning, he changed his tune. LaFluer told reporters Love’s ankle is a “little more sore” and that he’ll be out for at least week. He didn’t commit to Love returning for the Cardinals third preseason game, only that the 21-year old running back will be re-evaluated in a week. Love totaled 73 scrimmage yards and looked like the clear-cut starter against the Raiders on Thursday, but Tyler Allgeier could end up being the de facto starter if Love’s ankle injury lingers into the regular season.

item.title: Seahawks signed CB Devon Witherspoon to a four-year, $132 million contract extension.
item.description:
Devon Witherspoon SEA Cornerback

The deal includes $101 million guaranteed and makes Witherspoon the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history by both the total and average value of the contract. Witherspoon’s $132 million total value bests Rams CB Trent McDuffie, who signed a $124 million extension this offseason, for the biggest cornerback contract in the game. His $33 million per year average value overtakes Browns CB Denzel Ward’s $31.1 million for highest average value. Now attention should shift towards Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez, who appears to be next in line for an extension in this neighborhood.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez (undisclosed) won’t practice on Saturday.
item.description:
Christian Gonzalez NE Cornerback

Gonzalez missed practice on Tuesday, didn’t play in the Patriots’ preseason game on Thursday and remains off the field for Saturday’s practice. Still awaiting a contract extension from the Patriots, Gonzalez’ absence is related to an injury he suffered in practice last week, according to Patriots HC Mike Vrabel. While Gonzalez won’t practice, Vrabel said he’ll get treatment and work on conditioning, which implies the injury isn’t serious.

Source: Carlos A. Lopez

item.title: Bears WR Luther Burden (groin) was spotted running on the field before the Bears preseason game on Saturday.
item.description:
Luther Burden CHI Wide Receiver

Burden limped off the practice field a week ago and is expected to miss about a month with a groin injury. The injury isn’t considered serious and the hope is that he’ll be active for the Bears first regular season matchup against the Panthers in Week 1. Burden running on the field before the Bears first preseason game was a welcome sight for the organization and fantasy managers alike as the 22-year-old wide receiver appears to be progressing in his recovery.

Source: Chris Kwiecinski

item.title: Lions HC Dan Campbell told reporters WR Isaac TeSlaa is going to be just fine.
item.description:
Isaac TeSlaa DET Wide Receiver

Even after TeSlaa’s training camp struggles extended into the Lions’ first preseason game, Detroit doesn’t seem worried about the 24-year-old receiver. TeSlaa had his first target go through his hands and off his helmet for an interception and later couldn’t hang on to a fourth down pass in the loss to the Bengals on Thursday. Still, his only competitor for the WR3 role is Greg Dortch, a journeyman receiver who also failed to catch a pass in the first preseason game. The Lions WR3 isn’t likely to be a fantasy-relevant role when everyone else in the offense is healthy, but Detroit would still like to see more development from their third-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.

Source: Dave Birkett

item.title: Steelers signed DL Keeanu Benton to a four-year, $72 million contract extension.
item.description:
Keeanu Benton PIT Defensive Lineman

The deal was first reported by NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Benton, who turned 25 in July, is entering his fourth season in the league after the Steelers selected him in the second-round of the 2023 NFL Draft. Coming off a career-best season that saw him record 5.5 sacks, Benton would’ve been set to hit free agency next offseason without a contract extension. Now Benton joins LB Nick Herbig, TE Darnell Washington and K Chris Boswell on the list of Steelers to receive extensions this offseason. With his $18 million per year contract, Benton is now the highest-paid defensive lineman in Steelers history.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Jets WR Omar Cooper caught 2-of-3 targets for 31 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Omar Cooper NYJ Wide Receiver

Cooper entered the game on the Jets’ second drive, after the established starters called it a night. The usage meant Cooper played behind WR Isaiah Williams, who played 7-of-11 snaps on the first drive. Cooper continued playing through the Jets’ sixth drive. According to Rotoworld’s own Kyle Dvorchak, the last non-quarterback first-round rookie to play that late is former Titans WR Treylon Burks, back in his 2022 rookie season. This does not bode well for Cooper’s early-season usage.

Source: Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Buccaneers WR Ted Hurst caught 2-of-6 targets for 19 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Jets.
item.description:
Ted Hurst TB Wide Receiver

The Buccaneers rested their established starters, which takes a little shine off of Hurst’s start. Regardless, he led the team in targets through three drives and nearly hauled in a deep target after helpfully getting open during a scramble drill. The third-round rookie appeared to slip while diving for the catch, and he was unable to fully secure the pass before he and the ball hit the ground. Still, it was a decent start for him. He remains a worthwhile late-round dart throw.

item.title: Jets RB Braelon Allen rushed four times for 44 yards and one touchdown in Friday’s preseason game against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Braelon Allen NYJ Running Back

Allen stole one snap from starting RB Breece Hall on the first drive. Allen then stayed on the field for all of the second drive, breaking off a beautiful 31-yard touchdown run to put the Jets up 10-0 at the end of it. On his scoring play, Allen broke left at the snap before cutting it back and exploding through the line between the right guard and right tackle. It was a foot race to the end zone after that. The performance should solidify his grip on the RB2 role.

item.title: Dolphins WR Caleb Douglas caught 1-of-2 targets for 28 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Commanders.
item.description:
Caleb Douglas MIA Wide Receiver

Douglas is worth a late-round pick. Dolphins QB Malik Willis attempted five passes tonight, sending two his way. Both of Douglas’ targets were downfield throws. Douglas erred on the first. After managing to get wide open, running toward the right sideline, the rookie wide receiver experienced a blip in his spatial awareness and ended up securing the pass while stepping out of bounds. Willis gave him another chance on a vertical route from the slot, firing a long ball to the lanky receiver downfield. Douglas fought contact with his right hand while high-pointing the pass with his left, and critically retained possession as he landed hard on his back. The third-round rookie looks good.

item.title: Malik Willis completed 4-of-5 passes for 43 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Commanders, adding two rushes for nine yards.
item.description:
Malik Willis MIA Quarterback

Willis’ lone incompletion was not his fault. His intended receiver stepped out of bounds during the catch. The Dolphins’ new quarterback was not afraid to push the ball downfield and scrambled twice in Commanders territory. One carry occurred in the green zone, and Willis managed to break an attempted horse-collar tackle before being pushed out of bounds at the four-yard line. Willis won’t fool you into thinking he is an elite quarterback, but his dual-threat profile should yield QB1 spiked weeks this season.

item.title: De’Von Achane rushed seven times for 39 yards and one touchdown in Friday’s preseason game against the Commanders.
item.description:
De'Von Achane MIA Running Back

Spring and summer reports indicated that the Dolphins’ new coaching staff wanted to operate a run-heavy offense. Those reports weren’t lying. Achane took run after run up the middle until he punched one in from one yard out. Questions remain as to how efficient this offense might be, but Achane is seemingly set to handle a large workload again this season. Backup RB Jaylen Wright was the RB2 tonight, taking his first carry for 13 yards up the middle.

item.title: Broncos RB Jonah Coleman rushed four times for 24 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Jonah Coleman DEN Running Back

Coleman took a few snaps with tonight’s starters after replacing RB RJ Harvey on the second drive. Coleman picked up two first downs on the ground, barreling through contact on both plays. He earned one target as a receiver out of the backfield and took it for a five-yard gain. Unfortunately, the play was erased by a penalty, but it was good to see him get involved through the air regardless. Coleman looks like a capable player. He is worth speculatively stashing on fantasy benches at this time.

item.title: Cardinals OG Chase Bisontis will undergo surgery to repair a torn MCL in his knee and could miss the 2026 season.
item.description:
Chase Bisontis ARI Guard

The report comes from NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Bisontis is expected to miss most of the season and could end up missing all of it. Rapoport ambiguously adds that “only the MCL will be repaired,” leaving room for interpretation as to whether Bisontis’ knee took more damage in the injury. This is a very unfortunate situation for the second-round rookie. Hopefully, he makes a complete recovery and returns to form without issue.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Commanders QB Marcus Mariota exited Friday’s preseason game against the Dolphins after suffering an apparent knee injury.
item.description:
Marcus Mariota WAS Quarterback

Mariota appeared to injure his knee when he turned to hand the ball off to his running back, and immediately started limping. He was seemingly patting his right knee while sitting on the field, talking to trainers after the play. He was able to leave the field under his own power, but we do not expect him to return. He was replaced by QB Sam Hartman.

item.title: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said the team’s running back usage “is going to have to be a little bit more by committee” this season.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten JAC Running Back

Coen discussed both RB Bhayshul Tuten and RB Chris Rodriguez during his presser. Regarding Tuten, Coen said the second-year back has shown that he has “bought in” over the past year, and complimented his ability to take “hard coaching” while noting his 4.28-second 40 speed. Coen adds that Tuten has to continue working on making his reads and not overthinking things. Regarding Rodriguez, Coen complimented his recent downhill running and blitz pickups. Coen loves consistency at the running back position. This looks like it will be a committee to start the year. That said, if one player separates, things can change quickly. Tuten remains the high-upside pick, although Rodriguez can be productive in his own right.

Source: Jacksonville Jaguars

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that the Bills, Bears and 49ers are among the teams that have inquired about Bucs DT Vita Vea’s availability.
item.description:
Vita Vea TB Nose Tackle

Garafolo says that the Buccaneers remain steadfast in their position that Vea is not available. The team has also apparently kept the lines of communication open with Vea regarding a potential new deal, although “a deal is not imminent.” Vea is set to make roughly $18 million in the final year of his contract. Garafolo notes that the top of the defensive tackle market is now around $38 million annually, and Vea believes his production qualifies him for a contract extension in that tier.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes an expanded receiving role for Jaguars RB LeQuint Allen this season “seems legit.”
item.description:
LeQuint Allen

Allen’s pass-protection skills have him locked in as the Jaguars’ third-down running back. He played in all 17 games last season, but earned just 11 targets — hardly enough for a PPR-relevant role. Per Shipley, “has gotten more looks in the passing game in training camp this year than he did at this time a year ago.” He adds that it is unclear as to how much more involved Allen will be once the regular season arrives, but he closes by saying that “it does seem like the uptick is about to be very real.” With two other players expected to be involved in the backfield, it could still be tough for Allen to become FLEX-viable, but only time will tell.

Source: Sports Illustrated

item.title: The Tampa Bay Times’ Rick Stroud reports that the Buccaneers “are very optimistic” about WR Emeka Egbuka’s (toe) Week 1 availability.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Egbuka reportedly underwent more testing with a specialist today, who confirmed Ebuka indeed sprained his toe but determined that the injury is “stable.” This is great to hear. The second-year player is a high-ceiling WR2 candidate this season. The Buccaneers face the Bengals in Week 1, in what should be a fantasy-friendly environment.

Source: Rick Stroud

item.title: Jets QB Geno Smith (foot soreness) will not play in Friday’s preseason game against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Geno Smith NYJ Quarterback

NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that the team is not concerned about Smith’s foot soreness, writing, “if this was a regular-season game, he’d be a go.” Smith has reportedly been pushing the ball downfield in practice. Those hoping to catch a glimpse of the Jets’ passing attack will have to check back next week to see if the foot issue has been resolved. Rookie QB Cade Klubnik gets the start tonight.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Seahawks DE DeMarcus Lawrence said he plans to retire after the 2026 season.
item.description:
DeMarcus Lawrence SEA Linebacker

Lawrence was an impactful player on the Seahawks’ Super Bowl LX defense, leading the team in forced fumbles (five) and ranking in the top two in quarterback pressures (65) and sacks (10) across the full season. Lawrence, 34, should be a productive player once again this season.

Source: Jori Epstein

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is seeking multiple opinions on his recent injury.
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

Garafolo captioned a report from ESPN’s Katherine Terrell regarding Tyson’s new injury, adding that Tyson’s “timeline to return is TBD but doesn’t seem it’ll be anytime soon.” Here’s what we know: Tyson injured his right hamstring yesterday. Multiple right hamstring injuries derailed his 2025 college season and kept him from participating in the pre-draft process. Saints coach Kellen Moore initially said the new injury is unrelated to Tyson’s prior injuries, but New Orleans Football’s Mike Triplett noted today that Moore “changed his wording to say it wasn’t ‘necessarily’ related.” Moore also said that Tyson’s Week 1 availability may be impacted. Here’s hoping that Tyson’s decision to seek multiple opinions yields multiple positive reports. Stay tuned.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Kendall Lamm retired after 11 years in the NFL.
item.description:
Kendall Lamm HOU Tackle

The journeyman offensive lineman was on seven different teams over the course of his career. He initially entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Texans. He played for them for four seasons before making his way around parts of the league. Lamm had signed with the Ravens earlier this month, but they placed him on the reserve/retired list today.

Source: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk

item.title: Ravens activated LB Teddye Buchanan from the active/physically unable to perform list.
item.description:
Teddye Buchanan BAL Linebacker

Buchanan suffered a season-ending ACL tear in Week 15 last year. Before the injury, the then-rookie racked up 93 tackles, five TFLs, and 0.5 sacks. The Ravens correspondingly placed OT Kendall Lamm on the reserve/retired list.

Source: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk

item.title: NFL suspended Bills DT Phidarian Mathis for the first three regular season games.
item.description:
Phidarian Mathis BUF Defensive Tackle

The league determined that Mathis violated the Substances of Abuse Policy. The suspension begins on August 30th. He will be eligible to return on September 28th.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL suspended Titans DB Nazeeh Johnson for the first six games of the regular season.
item.description:
Nazeeh Johnson TEN Defensive Back

Johnson was found to have violated the Performance Enhancing Drug Policy. He signed with the Titans this offseason after appearing in one game for the Chiefs last year. He is likely to play a backup role in Tennessee this year.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: The Athletic’s Nicki Jhabvala reports that the NFL suspended Commanders DE Dorance Armstrong for the first game of the regular season.
item.description:
Dorance Armstrong WAS Defensive End

The league has ruled that Armstrong violated the league’s Personal Conduct Policy. Armstrong, 29, suffered a season-ending knee injury in October last year. He currently projects as a rotational edge rusher in Washington.

Source: Nicki Jhabvala

item.title: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said RB Josh Jacobs (groin) could “potentially” resume practicing late next week.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

Jacobs has been sidelined since August 6th and still faces a possible suspension from the NFL if the league determines that he violated the Personal Conduct Policy. He is still the starting running back in what has been an efficient offense, but 28-year-old running backs have certainly enjoyed better circumstances in the lead-up to a new season. He makes for a risky RB2 candidate at the moment.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi reports that the NFL suspended Falcons EDGE James Pearce for the first eight regular season games.
item.description:
James Pearce ATL Defensive End

The NFL determined that Pearce violated the league’s Personal Conduct Policy. He will be suspended without pay, but is allowed to participate in all preseason activities, including games. The suspension begins on August 30th, and he will be eligible for reinstatement on November 2nd. The Falcons go on bye in Week 11, so Week 9 marks his earliest possible return to the field. Pearce was arrested in February and initially charged with three felonies and one misdemeanor, including aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police, and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person.

Source: Marc Raimondi

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said that the 49ers “are pretty excited about WR De’Zhaun Stribling” after Thursday’s preseason performance.
item.description:
De'Zhaun Stribling SF Wide Receiver

Rapoport adds that Stribling’s “ability to catch basically everything has impressed.” The second-round rookie has soared since draft season. Once discussed as some film analysts’ preferred Day 1/2 options, Stribling now projects as a potentially reliable starter in the 49ers’ banged-up pass-catching corps.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Seahawks RB Jadarian Price (upper-leg soreness) participated in Friday’s walkthrough “after missing five of the previous six practices.”
item.description:
Jadarian Price SEA Running Back

This comes from The News Tribune’s Gregg Bell, who may be correcting the record on Price’s ailment. Price’s soreness has variously been reported as lower-body soreness, leg soreness, upper-body soreness and now upper-leg soreness. The young man has certainly been sore, and the upper-body report is not like the others. A leg issue is seemingly the most likely answer. Regardless, the Seahawks play their first preseason game tomorrow. Bell previously said it “doesn’t sound like” Price will be active, and today he emphasized that this was just a “light” walkthrough. If Price suits up, we might gain a little insight into the Seahawks’ intended running back rotation. If not, we will have to wait until the following week.

Source: Gregg Bell

item.title: Saints HC Kellen Moore said Jordyn Tyson is dealing with a right hamstring injury.
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

According to Moore, this is not related to the previous hamstring injuries Tyson has dealt with, and the team is gathering more information before determining a recovery timeline. Moore also said the possibility of Tyson missing Week 1 can’t be ruled out. It’s not exactly encouraging news, but we’re holding out hope that, at worst, this is a short-term absence for Tyson, whose pre-draft process was hampered by hamstring injuries. Tyson profiles as a decent WR3 play in fantasy if/when he is on the field this season.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said he expects Dont’e Thornton (undisclosed) to return at some point in the preseason.
item.description:
Dont'e Thornton LV Wide Receiver

Thornton has missed nearly a whole week of practice, paving the way for Jack Bech and rookie Malik Benson to see more reps. Kubiak said Thornton has “been banged up a little bit” this training camp, but did not go into further detail on his situation. Thornton caught 10 passes for 135 scoreless yards last season after generating plenty of camp hype. He is not on the fantasy radar at this time.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said “all three (QBs) deserve first team reps” this week after Thursday’s preseason game against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Fernando Mendoza LV Quarterback

Kubiak didn’t come right out and say Mendoza could see more first-team reps, but it feels like things are trending that way. His response came after he was asked if Mendoza specifically deserved more first-team reps after a nice outing in his first taste of preseason action, to which Kubiak said the team will put together a plan to ensure all three QBs get first-team reps, which feels somewhat evasive and unrealistic, given that we know career backup Aidan O’Connell isn’t contending for a starting job in camp. Kubiak went on record after Thursday’s game, saying that the battle for QB1 remains Kirk Cousins’ to lose. It wouldn’t be surprising if Mendoza did see more first-team reps in the coming days, but we would be surprised if O’Connell began working in with the first team. That said, it will be worth monitoring Mendoza’s first-team reps going forward, as he could still push Cousins for the starting role before Week 1.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Cardinals HC Mike LaFleur said he has ‘no concern’ over the rib injury that sidelined Carson Beck in Thursday’s preseason game against the Raiders.
item.description:
Carson Beck ARI Quarterback

LaFleur said Beck would have been well enough to throw if it were seven-on-seven drills, adding that the team “didn’t want to risk it” when it came to starting the rookie in Thursday’s preseason game. Beck already has some preseason experience under his belt. He threw for 188 yards and a touchdown in the Hall of Fame Game last week against the Panthers and will hopefully have a chance to suit up in next week’s preseason game against the Cowboys on Saturday.

Source: ProFootballTalk on NBCSports.com

item.title: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said “it’s his job to lose” when asked about Kirk Cousins’ status as QB1 after Thursday’s preseason game against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Kirk Cousins LV Quarterback

Cousins played on just one drive in Thursday’s loss. He went 5-for-6 on his pass attempts and capped his lone drive with a 13-yard touchdown pass to Michael Mayer. Rookie Fernando Mendoza, who looked sharp at times in his debut, is still positioned to open the season as Cousins’ backup, as Kubiak reasserted his decision to open the year with Cousins as the starter as of right now. Cousins has worked primarily with the starters in training camp and has received mostly good reports. It seems highly unlikely he would lose the starting job before Week 1’s game against the Dolphins.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Anthony Richardson completed 11-of-14 passes for 145 yards and an interception in Thursday’s preseason game against the Patriots, adding another six carries for 53 yards and a touchdown.
item.description:
Anthony Richardson IND Quarterback

Richardson’s interception came on a play in which the ball bounced off his receiver’s hands and into a defender’s arms. The former No. 4 overall pick was mostly solid on Thursday, making quick and decisive throws to his receivers while going a perfect 6-for-6 on pass attempts of 10-plus air yards. Richardson also lost a fumble on a 10-yard scramble in the second quarter, but made up for it later on a one-yard touchdown run on a QB sneak. His days as a Colt are likely numbered. Richardson stringing together a nice preseason could draw the interest of several QB-needy teams before the start of the season and position him to eventually see the field sometime in 2026.

item.title: Mike Washington rushed six times for 63 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Mike Washington Jr. LV Running Back

The rookie fourth-rounder wound up leading the Raiders in both rush attempts and rushing yards on Thursday, with his most notable run coming on a 53-yard burst that saw him evade multiple defenders on the play. Washington is competing for the Raiders’ RB2 spot behind Ashton Jeanty and should have the inside edge over third-year back Dylan Laube, who totaled 11 yards on five carries in Thursday’s loss.

item.title: Jack Bech caught 3-of-3 targets for 25 yards and a touchdown in Thursday’s preseason opener against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Jack Bech LV Wide Receiver

Two of Bech’s three receptions came with Fernando Mendoza under center. Mendoza threaded the needle twice to get the ball to the second-year receiver, with his first target to Bech resulting in a nine-yard gain to convert a third-and-eight. Mendoza would later find Bech for a short six-yard touchdown pass to give the Raiders their second touchdown of the night. Bech spent a significant amount of time playing with the backups, and his 20 snaps led all Raiders receivers on Thursday. Bech looked solid in this one and could be in line for a more meaningful role after a disappointing rookie year that saw him catch 20 passes for 224 scoreless yards.

item.title: Speaking after Thursday’s preseason opener, Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said second-round OG Chase Bisontis’ left knee injury was “not good.”
item.description:
Chase Bisontis ARI Guard

The No. 34 overall pick and projected starter appeared to be in a heap of pain upon going down in the third quarter. It’s a potentially brutal break for this woebegone franchise, though Friday’s testing could come back less severe than expected. If Bisontis is looking at a multi-month or season-ending absence it will likely force the Cardinals to dip into the free agent or back-end trade market.

Source: Darren Urban

item.title: Carnell Tate was held without a catch on three targets in Thursday’s preseason opener against the 49ers.
item.description:
Carnell Tate TEN Wide Receiver

Cam Ward played three series, but Tate was most active on the opening drive, playing 10-of-11 snaps (via NFL Network’s Michael F. Florio). The goose egg looks disappointing, of course, but it is utterly inconsequential. Slightly more concerning has been a hype-free start to Titans camp for the No. 4 overall pick, though he has been lauded for a few highlight plays of late. Emphasis on “a few,” we guess. It’s hard to muster too much concern, but then again, this was always likely to be a bumpy road for the Titans’ revamped offense this season. Tate is a WR3/4 with plenty of upside but “slow start” risk to match.

item.title: Fernando Mendoza completed 10-of-16 passes for 97 yards and a touchdown in Thursday’s preseason opener against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Fernando Mendoza LV Quarterback

Mendoza took over for Kirk Cousins on the Raiders’ second drive. New Raiders coach Klint Kubiak had Mendoza lining up under center and running play action, and the No. 1 overall pick responded by successfully threading the needle on tight window throws to both WR Malik Benson and Jack Bech. He also checked down to fellow rookie Mike Washington when needed. Mendoza’s score was a six-yard strike to Bech, with the second-year wideout turning the grab into a tumbling plunge into the end zone. It was a solid start for a rookie who is evidently going to begin the year on the bench.

item.title: Drew Allar completed 10-of-13 passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in Thursday’s preseason opener against the Packers, adding two rushes for two yards and a third score.
item.description:
Drew Allar PIT Quarterback

The controversial third-round pick is battling veteran Mason Rudolph and sophomore Will Howard for backup duties behind Aaron Rodgers. All three signal callers had strong outings against the Packers’ reserves on Thursday. A former massive recruit whose Penn State career did not go as planned, Allar has youth (22) and raw physical talent on his side as he looks to develop under Mike McCarthy. There is very little chance he would be ready for prime time if forced into 2026 action.

item.title: 49ers WR De’Zhaun Stribling caught 7-of-8 targets for 62 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Titans.
item.description:
De'Zhaun Stribling SF Wide Receiver

The 49ers rested their starters but let their second-round rookie play. Stribling lined up in the slot and out wide. He looked good winning contested targets and picking up yards after the catch, and showed no ill effects from the hamstring injury he dealt with earlier this month, which was nice to see. Rookie season FLEX treatment could be in play for him.

item.title: Jeremiyah Love rushed 11 times for 58 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Raiders, adding three receptions for 15 yards.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

Love apparently also picked up a minor ankle injury, but coach Mike LaFleur said he could have played through it were it the regular season. Whew. Love looked powerful and explosive against the Raiders tonight, at one point showing off a leaping spin move and later a hurdle. The first-round rookie running back out-snapped RB Tyler Allgeier 8-3 on the first drive with QB Jacoby Brissett. The two running backs continued rotating through the second drive, helmed by backup QB Gardner Minshew. Allgeier hung up his cleats after that, while Love played on 8-of-10 snaps on the third drive. If the first-drive snap count is any indication, Love may already have earned the clear-cut starting role in Arizona. His continued participation on the third drive clouds the picture. Hopefully we learn more next week.

item.title: Chargers TE Oronde Gadsden caught 2-of-3 targets for 21 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Texans.
item.description:
Oronde Gadsden II LAC Tight End

The second-year incumbent tight end is seemingly behind the Chargers’ free agent signee veteran TEs Charlie Kolar and David Njoku. Neither Kolar nor Njoku suited up this evening. Gadsden can still be viewed as a TE2/3 in best ball formats, but his current role could be undesirable for re-draft purposes.

item.title: Chargers RB Kimani Vidal rushed five times for eight yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Texans.
item.description:
Kimani Vidal LAC Running Back

Vidal stayed in for two drives and did not catch his only target. Tonight’s start suggests Vidal is behind RB Keaton Mitchell on the depth chart. Mitchell did not play, nor did starting RB Omarion Hampton. Vidal is a proven, capable fill-in starter, but he should only be drafted as the Chargers’ RB3 at this time.

item.title: Lionis WR Isaac TeSlaa caught 0-of-3 targets in Thursday’s preseason game against the Bengals.
item.description:
Isaac TeSlaa DET Wide Receiver

The Lions’ established starters did not play. Lions WR Greg Dortch could be challenging TeSlaa’s WR3 role, although Dortch went 0-for-1 as a receiver as well. TeSlaa out-snapped him 15-7 on the first three drives. TeSlaa took two more snaps on the fourth drive, sans Dortch, which ended in a turnover. This is a position battle to keep an eye on.

item.title: Bengals WR Andrei Iosivas caught 2-of-2 targets for 20 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Lions.
item.description:
Andrei Iosivas CIN Wide Receiver

Iosivas was on the field for two drives, taking 10 of the first 13 snaps and playing alongside QB Joe Burrow. Fourth-round rookie WR Colbie Young subbed in, taking one snap on the second drive and remained on the field after the starters left. He looked good hauling in a 20-yard gain on 3rd-and-16 from QB Joe Flacco. The battle for the Bengals’ WR3 role continues with Iosivas seemingly ahead of the rookie.

item.title: Packers WR Jayden Reed caught 1-of-2 targets for 19 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Steelers.
item.description:
Jayden Reed GB Wide Receiver

Reed played 7-of-9 snaps on the first drive before calling it a night. He was in the slot for all seven snaps. Reed snagged a 19-yard pass via a post route from the slot on 3rd-and-5. He was targeted again on a corner route just outside the end zone on 3rd-and-4 from the Steelers’ 19-yar4d line, but the pass was broken up. Packers WR Matthew Golden led the first-team offense with nine snaps.

item.title: Seahawks signed CB Terrion Arnold, formerly of the Lions.
item.description:
Terrion Arnold SEA Cornerback

ESPN’s Adam Schefter notes that the NFL must decide whether to put Arnold on the Commissioner’s Exempt List regarding his February arrest in relation to a robbery and kidnapping. Arnold reportedly has eight pending felony charges. The Lions drafted Arnold in the 2024 NFL Draft’s first round. They waived him in June. He notched four pass breakups and one interception in eight games last year.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Speaking on NFL Daily about his backfield rotation, Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said, “if a player is playing really well, I’m not going to take them out.”
item.description:
Omarion Hampton LAC Running Back

Earlier this week, McDaniel said he plans to employ a hot-hand approach at the running back position and plans to “use all three of those guys probably every game.” NFL Daily co-hosts Gregg Rosenthal and Jourdan Rodrigue helpfully followed up on those comments, specifically regarding their fantasy football implications. McDaniel encouragingly prefaced his response by saying, “no one has to worry,” adding that benching productive players is “bad business.” If you were already bullish on one or more of Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal, these comments can be taken positively. Reading between the lines, if Hampton, the starter, proves his value as the team’s RB1, he should receive a fantasy-friendly workload.

Source: Gregg Rosenthal

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Packers TE Tucker Kraft (knee) is on track to play in Week 1 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Tucker Kraft GB Tight End

According to Rapoport, the “biggest question” Kraft faces is whether he will get a contract extension that makes him the highest-paid tight end in the NFL before the season kicks off. Kraft led the team in receptions (16) and receiving yards (225) when he suffered a season-ending ACL tear in Week 9 last year. At 25 years old, he is early in his prime.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Cam Ward completed 5-of-12 passes for 57 yards in Thursday’s preseason opener against the 49ers, adding a two-yard rush.
item.description:
Cam Ward TEN Quarterback

Ward, who played three series, didn’t offer up many highlights, but he did help author a 95-yard touchdown drive on the Titans’ opening series vs. the 49ers’ backups. Learning a new offensive system as he breaks in a heavily revamped supporting cast, it’s not a surprise tonight was a “growing pains” effort even if it came against the second and third string. If Ward plays in the Titans’ second preseason game, it will be against the defending champion Seahawks.

item.title: ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reports that Packers QB Jordan Love will start in the team’s preseason Week 1 game against the Steelers.
item.description:
Jordan Love GB Quarterback

Although a potential, albeit brief, matchup against Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers is intriguing, the Packers’ wide receiver rotation is the real reason to tune in. Packers WR Christian Watson should be the team’s top target earner this season, and Love said WR Matthew Golden is set to assume X-receiver duties. Will slot WR Jayden Reed get to take snaps in two-receiver sets? That is to be determined.

Source: Brooke Pryor

item.title: ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reports that Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers could play one or two series in the team’s preseason Week 1 game against the Packers.
item.description:
Aaron Rodgers PIT Quarterback

Rodgers may not play at all, and reports indicate that he, personally, could go either way on the matter. Steelers coach Mike McCarthy plans to play quarterbacks in three groups. The first two will split first-half reps, while the third plays for the entire second half. Shortly after this report, during pre-game warmups, Pryor said that “all signs are pointing to Rodgers being on the bench tonight.”

Source: Brooke Pryor
